This study introduces a novel selective labeling strategy for semi-supervised learning that leverages the inherent correlations among data points. Our method identifies the most valuable samples by aggregating the predictions of a simple ensemble of models, each trained on a distinct subset of unlabeled data. We demonstrate that this approach outperforms state-of-the-art techniques on several benchmark datasets.

The joint detection of gravitational and electromagnetic waves from neutron star mergers offers a unique opportunity to study the interplay between strong gravity and electromagnetism. This paper examines the electromagnetic radiation generated by a charged, rotating black hole merging with a neutron star, utilizing the linearized approximation of the Einstein-Maxwell equations. Our findings indicate that, within this framework, the emitted electromagnetic energy is negligible compared to the total radiated gravitational energy. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the electromagnetic contribution to the gravitational waveform is minimal, suggesting that current detectors are unlikely to observe such effects.

Social determinants of health (SDOH) are critical factors influencing patient well-being, yet the information regarding these determinants is often scattered across clinical documentation. This study introduces a novel framework designed to extract SDOH information from electronic health records (EHRs) using natural language processing (NLP) techniques. We developed a multi-stage pipeline that leverages conditional random fields (CRF) and a support vector machine (SVM) classifier to identify and categorize SDOH mentions. Our approach successfully identified 1,000 distinct SDOH categories, achieving a macro F1 score of 0.79. Furthermore, we created a hierarchical taxonomy to organize these mentions, which can facilitate the development of robust SDOH extraction tools and support broader research initiatives.

We examine the energetic cost of repositioning a self-propelled particle between two fixed locations by varying the frequency of switching in its swimming dynamics. Our analysis reveals that the cost exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on switching frequency, characterized by a minimum that occurs at an intermediate rate. This optimal frequency is determined by the interplay between the swimmer's internal noise and the external environmental noise. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the cost can be minimized by an order of magnitude compared to constant swimming modes by strategically tuning this intermediate switching frequency.

This study examines the long-term consequences of the pandemic on the variety of urban interactions and the capacity of communities to endure challenges. By analyzing a dataset of 1.5 million geotagged tweets collected from 2019 to 2021, the research investigates how the variety of social interactions changed throughout the pandemic. The findings indicate that the diversity of urban encounters declined significantly during the crisis, a trend that persisted well into 2021, even after mobility patterns had returned to pre-pandemic levels. Furthermore, the study reveals that this reduction in interaction variety was not uniform across all areas; it was more pronounced in cities with lower initial diversity and in neighborhoods characterized by higher socioeconomic segregation. These disparities suggest that the pandemic may have exacerbated existing urban inequalities, thereby weakening the overall resilience of certain communities.

We present a three-dimensional, three-fluid, hydrodynamic simulation of a circumstellar disc containing a migrating object, specifically designed to investigate the inner disc dynamics near a high-mass young stellar object (MYSO). Our study examines a 10 Jupiter-mass ($10 M_{\rm Jup}$) planet orbiting at 10 astronomical units (au) within a disc with a 1000 solar mass ($1000 M_{\odot}$) core and a 1000-au radius. The simulation reveals that the migrating planet triggers a spiral density wave, which generates a shock at the inner edge of the disc. This shock causes a significant temperature increase, leading to a substantial reduction in the inner disc's surface density. Furthermore, the inner disc exhibits a distinct two-armed spiral structure, with the innermost 10 au displaying a prominent spiral arm. The simulation also demonstrates that the migrating planet induces a two-armed spiral pattern in the disc's angular velocity, with the innermost 100 au showing a two-armed spiral structure in the angular velocity. Finally, the simulation indicates that the migrating planet induces a two-armed spiral pattern in the disc's angular velocity, with the innermost 100 au displaying a two-armed spiral structure in the angular velocity.

This work introduces a general framework for scattering theory applicable to a broad class of quantum systems. The core of this approach involves characterizing the scattering process through the asymptotic algebra and the scattering matrix. We demonstrate that the asymptotic algebra is isomorphic to the algebra of local observables defined on the causal complement of a specific wedge region. Furthermore, we establish a one-to-one correspondence between the unitary representations of the asymptotic algebra and the irreducible representations of the system.

This study examines the exposure risks posed by 5G cellular infrastructure, specifically analyzing the impact of building attenuation on both 5G and legacy systems. The research utilizes a dataset of 1.5 million measurements collected across the Netherlands to derive building attenuation models for various 5G frequency bands. The analysis reveals that, when accounting for these attenuation effects, the exposure from 5G towers is comparable to that of pre-5G technology. Furthermore, the study indicates that the majority of exposure incidents occur in urban centers, where the density of base stations is high, resulting in low individual exposure levels.

This study examines the inverse surface elevation problem for two-dimensional, irrotational, incompressible water waves with a flat free surface. We demonstrate that reconstructing the surface elevation from the wave envelope is sufficient to uniquely determine the velocity potential. Furthermore, we present an explicit reconstruction formula for the potential based on the envelope.
This paper presents a proof of the surface layer theorem applicable to differential forms within the context of locally convex spaces.

This paper introduces a layered control system designed for mobile platforms utilizing sonar sensors to navigate autonomously in unknown environments. The architecture comprises three distinct layers: a low-level layer manages the direct control of actuators, a mid-level layer executes obstacle avoidance maneuvers, and a high-level layer handles path planning. The proposed method was validated through a series of experiments conducted in an uncharted setting, demonstrating the system's efficacy.

This study introduces a novel approach to fake news detection that leverages contextual information from social media platforms. We propose a new framework, Contextual Fake News Detection (CFND), which operates in two stages: first, it extracts relevant contextual cues from a news source's surrounding content, and second, it classifies the news item as either authentic or false. To achieve this, we developed a new dataset comprising 1,000 fake news articles from Facebook, each paired with its corresponding contextual context. Experimental results indicate that our model outperforms state-of-the-art methods by a significant margin, achieving a 10% improvement in F1 score.

We examine the impact of curvature on the phase transition within a two-dimensional Ising model on a square lattice by incorporating a curvature-dependent modification to the system's entropy. Our findings indicate that curvature influences both the transition temperature and the transition order. Specifically, increasing curvature induces a shift from a first-order to a second-order phase transition. Concurrently, the curvature effect drives a reduction in the system's entropy change, which correlates with diminished magnetization change and the appearance of hysteresis.

This study introduces a suboptimal decoding order policy grounded in a Markov decision process (MDP) framework. By employing a finite state-space and finite state-transition approach, the method circumvents the prohibitive computational demands associated with the exact solution of the full MDP. Numerical simulations demonstrate that this suboptimal strategy achieves performance nearly identical to the optimal policy, yet it reduces complexity to a level that is independent of the total number of users.

This work introduces a novel, low-complexity algorithm designed to solve the two-block reformulation of the rotationally invariant L1-PCA problem. By employing a Gauss-Seidel approach, the method alternates between updating a single column of a matrix and a single row of a vector. The convergence of this algorithm is established through a rigorous proof demonstrating that each update step strictly increases the objective function. Furthermore, the paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the computational complexity for both individual iterations and the entire process.

We propose a novel self-training approach for semantic labeling that leverages paraphrase tasks to autonomously generate pseudo-labels. Our method introduces a new pseudo-labeling strategy that creates pseudo-supervision by aggregating predictions from a teacher model trained on paraphrased versions of original images. This framework is designed to enhance the robustness of self-training against noisy pseudo-labels. Specifically, we introduce a pseudo-label filtering mechanism that leverages the inherent redundancy among paraphrase-derived pseudo-labels to eliminate unreliable predictions. Experimental results on the Cityscapes dataset demonstrate that our method achieves a mIoU of 77.1%, surpassing the baseline self-training performance of 75.5% by a margin of 1.6%.

A half-positional winning condition is defined as one where a player can secure victory using a strategy that depends only partially on history, with the extent of this dependency varying according to the specific condition. This paper investigates the minimal amount of memory required for a player to win under combined conditions formed by unions of half-positional half-winning criteria. We demonstrate that if these criteria are also prefix-independent, the resulting condition remains half-positional. Conversely, we show through counterexamples that these requirements are essential: removing prefix-independence can lead to a non-half-positional union, and omitting the half-positivity of an individual condition can result in a union requiring infinite memory. Finally, we establish that whenever these conditions are met, the resulting half-positional condition can be expressed as a specific finite combination of prefix-independent half-positional conditions, where the memory needed for each component is strictly bounded.

We present X-ray spectral analyses for four asynchronous polar systems—AM Her, V445 Oph, V447 Oph, and V449 Oph—utilizing archival data from the Rossi X-ray Timing Explorer (RXTE) and the XMM-Newton observatories. Our findings indicate that the X-ray spectra of these asynchronous systems are comparable to those of standard polar systems, exhibiting similar spectral characteristics. Specifically, the spectra are well-modeled by a two-component approach comprising a thermal disk component and a non-thermal power-law component. Furthermore, the power-law indices and disk temperatures derived for these asynchronous systems align closely with values observed in typical polar systems.

Partitioned fluid-structure interaction (FSI) methods treat the fluid and solid sub-problems independently, utilizing an iterative scheme to couple them. This study examines a specific class of fully implicit partitioned algorithms where the solid is solved with a single time step, while the fluid employs multiple sub-steps within each global iteration. We establish the convergence of these schemes under the condition that the fluid and solid sub-cycles are consistent. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the convergence rate is independent of the number of fluid sub-steps used per iteration.

This work introduces HiTMap, a novel navigation representation that merges the benefits of global metric maps and tile-based maps. Unlike traditional global metric maps, which often struggle with scalability and efficiency, HiTMap achieves this by dividing the environment into tiles that are compressed into compact vectors. These tiles are organized within a hierarchical tree structure, enabling the representation to adapt dynamically to the agent's current position and navigation goals. This design allows for a seamless balance between global awareness and localized precision. Evaluation results demonstrate that HiTMap outperforms standard tile-based maps in navigation performance while maintaining comparable performance to global metric maps.

This research introduces a system designed to identify abusive material in tweets, utilizing a deep learning approach based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). The model was trained on a dataset comprising 100,000 labeled tweets, with an additional 20,000 held out for evaluation. The system achieved a macro F1 score of 0.8000, demonstrating its effectiveness in detecting hate speech and abusive content.

Atomic interferometry has emerged as a highly sensitive technique for detecting local magnetic fields, capable of reaching sensitivities up to $10^{-14}$ T/$\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$ in specific configurations. This study demonstrates that by integrating a local field detector with a global field sensor, one can achieve a sensitivity of $10^{-15}$ T/$\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$ for detecting local fields. This enhancement is realized by leveraging the sensor's ability to measure minute field variations caused by the local source, thereby isolating the local field from the dominant background field. This method was validated through experiments using a Helmholtz coil to generate a local field, which yielded a measured sensitivity of $10^{-15}$ T/$\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$.

We propose a magnetothermoelectric heterostructure composed of a magnetic topological insulator (such as MnBi$_2$Te$_4$) and a normal topological insulator (such as Cr-doped (Bi,Sb)$_2$Te$_3$). This design leverages the magnetocaloric effect to generate distinct thermal responses for spin-up and spin-down carriers, thereby enabling spin-selective magnetothermal transport. By varying the magnetization of the magnetic topological insulator, the sign of the spin-dependent Seebeck coefficient can be reversed, creating a spin-dependent magnetothermal switch. Furthermore, the spin-dependent Nernst effect is predicted to be significantly enhanced by the magnetocaloric effect. These findings offer a pathway to engineer spin-thermoelectric devices with tunable functionalities.

This study introduces an enhanced effective gap width methodology for modeling light propagation through planar-parallel dielectric plates, specifically addressing the limitations of local approaches by incorporating the influence of incident angle. This enhancement is achieved by integrating the gap width concept with the transverse mode matching technique. The resulting framework is validated against rigorous coupled wave analysis (RCWA) and demonstrates superior accuracy in predicting the angular dependence of transmission and reflection coefficients, particularly for high-contrast multilayer stacks. Furthermore, this approach is applied to analyze the spectral response of a Bragg mirror, revealing a significant improvement in the precision of stopband edge locations.

Although the calculus of constructions, introduced by Gérard Huet and Thierry Coquard, has profoundly influenced numerous aspects of type theory and programming languages, its formalization within Isabelle/HOL remains incomplete. This paper presents the first formalization of the calculus of constructions in Isabelle/HOL, encompassing both dependent function and inductive types.

This work introduces a novel approach to quantum electronics, utilizing entanglement concepts to analyze the interaction between a single electron and a quantum dot. We specifically examine two entanglement measures: the correlator method and the von-Neumann density-matrix technique. By applying these frameworks, we derive the effective Hamiltonian for a quantum dot containing one electron. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the resulting effective Hamiltonians are consistent with established results found in the literature.

We introduce a novel methodology for estimating admixture proportions from population-level genetic data by placing a Dirichlet process prior directly on admixture weights. This approach allows for the discovery of the true number of ancestral source populations and the identification of which sources contribute to each target population. We demonstrate that this framework recovers identifiable admixture weights even when the number of sources is overparameterized, a scenario where traditional methods relying on fixed-dimensional Dirichlet priors fail. Furthermore, we show that this method effectively handles cases where multiple ancestral sources share identical genetic profiles.

We examine the two-loop anomalous dimensions of twist-four operators within the AdS$_5 \times$ S$^5$ superstring context. By analyzing the two-loop correction to the four-gluon scattering amplitude in $\mathcal{N}=4$ Super Yang-Mills theory, we identify the specific linear combinations of twist-four operators that correspond to the leading singularities of this amplitude. Our findings indicate that these anomalous dimensions are consistent with the double-copy structure of the amplitude, a result that aligns with the expectations derived from the dual conformal bootstrap approach.

GPU memory allocators are critical for optimizing performance and ensuring efficient memory usage in deep learning. However, existing approaches often rely on rigid, static memory layouts that fail to accommodate the dynamic nature of real-world applications. To address this limitation, we introduce DynaSOAr, a novel GPU memory allocator that leverages dynamic memory layouts to enhance both performance and utilization. Our approach employs a hybrid allocation strategy that combines a global allocator with per-process allocators, enabling each process to manage its own memory layout independently. Additionally, DynaSOAr utilizes a layout-aware memory compaction technique to optimize memory layouts by reducing fragmentation. Comprehensive evaluations across various deep learning workloads demonstrate that DynySOAr achieves a 1.15x speedup compared to the cuMem allocator while improving memory utilization by 1.14x.

This study investigates the boundedness of the $p$-potential operator acting on generalized mixed Morrey spaces. This study examines the influence of spin-orbit coupling on the electronic states of magnetic adatoms or dimers atop superconducting surfaces, utilizing a tight-binding framework to calculate the local density of states (LDOS) via scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) simulations. Our findings indicate that spin-orbit coupling significantly alters the LDOS patterns associated with Yu-Shiba-Rusinov (YSR) states, specifically shifting the locations of their peaks and anti-nodes. This effect is observed to be highly sensitive to the spin-orbit coupling strength, the magnetic moment of the adatoms, and the atomic arrangement. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these spin-orbit induced modifications can be leveraged to enhance the spatial resolution of STM imaging for YSR states, thereby facilitating more precise determinations of the underlying magnetic configuration.

Implicit functions are increasingly utilized in computer vision to represent complex shapes, offering advantages such as compactness and differentiability. However, these functions typically require optimization to produce high-resolution masks, a process that is computationally expensive and incompatible with real-time applications. To address this limitation, we introduce FourierMask, a method that leverages the inherent properties of the Fourier domain to generate high-resolution segmentation masks directly without optimization. Specifically, FourierMask employs a Fourier-based implicit function that encodes a shape's boundary as a Fourier series, while its corresponding interior is defined by a radial function relative to that boundary. By leveraging the inherent differentiability of Fourier series and radial functions, we derive an analytical gradient for the implicit function, enabling the direct computation of high-resolution masks through backpropagation. Experiments demonstrate that FourierMask achieves a 1000x speedup compared to prior methods, delivering a 1000x faster inference speed than previous approaches while maintaining comparable performance. Furthermore, the method supports end-to-end training for joint segmentation and pose estimation, yielding state-of-the-art results on both the COCO and MPII datasets.

This work demonstrates that the existence of bounded, complete minimal disks in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with prescribed boundary is guaranteed whenever the boundary is a compact, minimal submanifold of a Euclidean space with a specific discrete spectrum.

This study introduces a novel method for segmenting clouds in satellite images by modeling the cloud structure as a superposition of a visible layer and an underlying "veiled core." This core is defined as a hidden, three-dimensional cloud system obscured by the visible layer, with its presence inferred from the visible layer's thickness. The proposed approach employs a probabilistic framework to estimate the core's 3D geometry and the visible layer's thickness using a Maximum Likelihood Estimation technique. Validation against a dataset of 1,000 cloud images demonstrates that the method achieves a Mean Absolute Error of 0.11 pixels in estimating the visible layer thickness and 0.13 pixels in reconstructing the core's 3D shape.

We investigate the interaction of a negatively chirped laser pulse with a two-layer target consisting of a primary solid foil and a secondary coating of very low density and minimal thickness. Our findings indicate that this configuration generates a significantly stronger, temporally varying magnetic field compared to a single solid foil. This field drives the acceleration of ions from the rear surface of the primary foil. Specifically, the magnetic field strength increases as the laser pulse chirp tightens, reaching a maximum when the chirp duration is approximately 100 femtoseconds. Additionally, the field strength is inversely proportional to the density of the secondary layer. This mechanism enables the generation of ions with energies up to 100 MeV/u, a result that aligns well with both experimental data and theoretical models.

We report the discovery of three transiting mini-Neptunes orbiting the nearby K-dwarf star TOI-270 (TOI-270b, c, and d), identified via TESS photometry and confirmed through radial velocity measurements obtained with the HARPS-N and HIRES spectrographs. These planets reside within or near the system's habitable zone, with TOI-270c specifically located at 0.71 AU, receiving stellar irradiation comparable to Earth's ($S_{\star} = 0.68 S_{\oplus}$). While the outer planets (b and c) possess masses of 4.8 and 10.8 Earth masses respectively, the innermost planet (d) is significantly smaller at 0.39 Earth masses, with a radius of 0.41 Earth radii. This low mass-to-radius ratio for TOI-270d suggests a rocky composition, potentially indicating a rocky super-Mercury.

We have investigated the electronic and magnetic properties of carbon and nitrogen impurities in TiO$_2$ by substituting them into either octahedral or tetrahedral sites. Our findings indicate that carbon and nitrogen exhibit distinct behaviors depending on their location: interstitial carbon and nitrogen are paramagnetic, whereas their substitutional counterparts form antiferromagnetic dimers. Furthermore, the magnetic moments of interstitial carbon and nitrogen are notably higher than those of their substitutional equivalents.

This study examines the potential for detecting flavor-changing neutral top quark decays, specifically $t \to Zh$ and $t \to W^{\pm}h^{\mp}$, through semi-inelastic scattering channels characterized by a single $W$ boson in the final state. These semi-elastic signatures are identified as $t \to W^{\pm}b \to W^{\pm}W^{\mp}h^{\mp}$ and $t \to W^{\pm}b \to W^{\pm}W^{\mp}h^{\mp}$, where the $h^{\mp}$ boson subsequently decays into a pair of leptons. The analysis utilizes the full dataset collected by the ATLAS detector at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 139 fb$^{-1}$. No statistically significant excess above the Standard Model background predictions is observed. Consequently, the analysis establishes upper limits on the branching ratios for $t \to Zh$ and $t \to W^{\pm}h^{\mp}$ at 95% confidence level, with values of less than 0.011 and less than 0.005, respectively.

The X-ray Integral Field Unit (X-IFU), a next-generation instrument aboard the European Space Agency's Athena mission, will enable the study of turbulence within the intra-cluster medium (ICM) by detecting shock waves and ripples. This analysis relies on the instrument's high spectral resolution to measure Doppler shifts in X-ray emission lines, thereby revealing turbulent velocities. This manuscript presents a simulation of X-IFU observations of the Perseus cluster, utilizing a high-resolution, three-dimensional, magnetohydrodynamic simulation that incorporates radiative cooling and magnetic fields. The simulation data were processed to generate a synthetic X-IFU dataset, which was subsequently analyzed to determine the feasibility of detecting turbulence. Our findings indicate that X-IFU can measure turbulent velocities in the core of the Perseus cluster with a precision of approximately 10 km/s over a 100 ks observation period. Furthermore, the instrument is capable of detecting individual shock waves and ripples, as well as the cluster's overall turbulent velocity field.

This paper presents a new proof establishing the bound $c'(G, F) \geqslant \frac{|E(G)|}{\Delta_F}$ for the generalized edge coloring problem, where $\Delta_F$ denotes the maximum degree of any subgraph formed by $F$ edges. Specifically, we demonstrate that if $\frac{|E(G)|}{\Delta_F}$ is an integer, then $c'(G, F) = \frac{|E(G)|}{\Delta_F}$ holds true whenever $F$ is a triangle.

We present a new analysis of the density structure within the Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) of our galaxy, utilizing a sample of 1,000 tracers from the Spitzer Legacy Infrared Molecular Emission Line Survey (SILES). By analyzing the two-point correlation function of these sources, we determine that the CMZ exhibits anisotropy on scales ranging from 10 to 100 parsecs, with the degree of anisotropy decreasing as scale increases. This finding aligns with previous results derived from dust emission data. Furthermore, we observe that the density structure is anisotropic along the Galactic disk direction, a characteristic that becomes more pronounced at smaller scales.

This paper introduces a novel eye-focused detection system designed to identify eyes within images, distinguishing itself by relying solely on eye features rather than requiring the full face. This approach offers a significant advantage over existing methods, which are often hindered by low image quality or occlusion when facial details are unavailable. To achieve this, we developed a specialized dataset comprising 10,000 images centered on eyes, and we propose a new loss function specifically for eye detection tasks. Our method was evaluated against current state-of-the-art approaches, demonstrating superior performance with a 0.02 increase in mAP and a 0.01 improvement in F1 score.

This study examines the resilience of qubits and qutrits against noise during mass measurement, utilizing a specific error model characterized by a mixture of bit-flip and phase-shift operations. Our findings indicate that qutrits exhibit superior noise tolerance compared to qubits, with mass determination accuracy improving as the energy gap between qutrit levels increases. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this advantage is contingent upon the noise profile; specifically, qutrits outperform qubits when the error rates affecting the lower and upper levels differ, whereas qubits may be more robust if the error rates are identical.

We report a positron polarization degree exceeding 30% utilizing a spin-selective positron filter based on the resonant annihilation of positrons with ortho-hydrogen. This technique enables the generation of highly polarized positrons with a degree surpassing 30%, a level deemed critical for advancing positron physics and facilitating applications in fundamental research and medical positron emission tomography (PET).

We demonstrate that groups with polynomial diameter, specifically those where the diameter of maximal nilpotent subgroups grows as a polynomial relative to the degree of the group, necessarily possess a finite number of conjugacy classes of such subgroups. As a consequence, it follows that groups with polynomial diameter are finite-by-abelian-by-finite, implying they also have a finite number of conjugacy classes of maximal abelian subgroups.

This study introduces a novel, non-invasive temperature sensor utilizing a deep learning-based image processing technique. The proposed method employs a convolutional neural network (CNN) to identify and segment the skin region in images, subsequently calculating the temperature via a linear regression model. This approach was tested on 1,000 images captured from 50 individuals using a smartphone equipped with a 16-megapixel camera. The results indicate that the sensor achieves a resolution of 0.15°C and an inaccuracy of 0.38°C, with a linear regression coefficient of determination ($R^2$) of 0.99. These findings demonstrate that the proposed sensor offers a cost-effective, high-precision solution for temperature measurement.

We examine the linear stability of a rotating, incompressible, electrically conducting fluid within a spherical domain, subject to rigid boundary conditions and driven by a magnetic field composed of mutually supportive toroidal and poloidal elements. Our analysis reveals that the fluid remains stable against infinitesimal perturbations whenever the toroidal and poloidal components are aligned in a specific manner. Conversely, we demonstrate that introducing a slight misalignment between these components can induce instability, even in scenarios that were previously stable.

We demonstrate that the analogy between the renormalization group equations and fluid dynamics is sufficiently robust to allow for the derivation of rigorous, universal lower bounds on the irreversibility inherent in RG trajectories. By applying this framework to the three-dimensional Gross-Neveu model, we derive a bound for the irreversibility ratio that surpasses all previously established results.

Discovering the specific song that matches a set of lyrics is often more efficient via a lyric-focused search engine than navigating standard web results. Although several such engines exist, they frequently lack robust support for locating both the audio and corresponding lyrics of a target track. This paper introduces LyricSearch, a novel system designed to facilitate finding music through lyric-based queries. Leveraging a large-scale dataset of over 100 million song-lyric pairs, the system employs a dual-encoder architecture to embed both audio and text, utilizing cosine similarity to perform rapid, exact-match retrieval. Furthermore, the authors present LyricBERT, a new model specifically trained to represent lyrics within an audio-lyric dual space. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach achieves a 99.9% recall rate when identifying songs from exact lyric inputs, significantly outperforming existing methods.

We demonstrate that a topological groupoid extension by a topological group corresponds precisely to a $\mathcal{G}$-valued 2-cocycle, which in turn defines a $\mathcal{G}$-germ on the quotient stack associated with the extension.
